title: Recap: *-va/-ve* clauses in a history text

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know the adverbial participle in *-va/-ve* from B1 Unit 29 and from earlier C1 units. In a history text it means 'having done X', and the person or group that did X is the subject of the main clause: *A földet felosztva az állam átalakította a falusi társadalmat.*

sections.title: When not to use it
sections.content: If the two clauses have different subjects, use a full clause with *miután*, which you know from B1 Unit 1.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A földet felosztva az állam átalakította a falusi társadalmat.
Having divided the land, the state transformed village society.
A vagyonukat elveszítve sok nemesi család állami hivatalba ment.
Having lost their wealth, many noble families went into state office.
A feudális kötelékeket megszüntetve a társadalom elindult a polgárosodás útján.
Having abolished the feudal ties, society set out on the path of embourgeoisement.
